sources.entry: TRex - TRex is the easiest way to copy the uncopyable text from images, YouTube videos, Zoom calls and more. If you can see it - you can copy it. TRex captures any text right into your Clipboard with magic of OCR.

summary.one_liner: TRex is a macOS menu bar app that captures text from any area of the screen using offline OCR and copies it straight to the clipboard.
summary.what_it_does: TRex lives in the macOS menu bar and is triggered via the menu or a configurable global shortcut. You select a screen area as you would for a screenshot, and the recognized text lands in the clipboard. It also reads QR codes and barcodes, and supports a configurable recognition language and a custom words list. Automation options include running a Shortcut, opening URLs found in QR codes or captured text, and triggering user-defined URL schemes. A CLI tool is bundled inside the app, and the app exposes trex:// URL scheme commands for capture, clipboard capture, automation, and preferences. The README says all features work offline.
use_cases: copy text from a non-selectable PDF
copy text from a YouTube video frame
copy text from a Zoom screen share
read QR codes and barcodes on screen
script text capture from the command line or other apps
how_to_run: Alternatively, buy TRex from the Mac App Store or download it from GitHub Releases
Launch TRex, then invoke Capture from the menu bar or with the global shortcut
Select the screen area containing the text; the text is placed in the clipboard
notable: Fully offline OCR, with no internet connection needed
Invisible by design: only a menu bar app and preferences, no other UI
Bundled CLI tool and trex:// URL scheme for automation
Official Alfred workflow and Raycast script commands
Available via Mac App Store, GitHub Releases, or Homebrew
caveats: Requires macOS Big Sur (11.0) or later
App Store version is a paid purchase
Raycast integration requires downloading the repository ZIP and adding the script directory manually
